transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?
I'm here today because I've been struggling with constant, uncontrollable worry and anxiety almost every day for about 11 months now. It has just become too difficult to manage on my own.
What kinds of things do you find yourself worrying about the most?

It isn't just one specific thing, honestly. My worries seem to spread to almost every part of my life, from my performance at work and school to my family's well-being and our finances. It feels like no matter what I'm doing, there is always something to worry about in every area.
Along with this constant worry, have you been experiencing physical symptoms like muscle tension, restlessness, fatigue, or trouble sleeping?

Yes, the muscle tension has been really bad; my neck, shoulders, and jaw feel constantly knotted and painful, and my whole body just feels stiff and easily fatigued. I'm not as sure about restlessness or sleep issues, but this physical stiffness is definitely very prominent.
Alongside the anxiety, have you also been feeling persistently down or depressed, or lost interest in activities you usually enjoy?

No, I haven't really been feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in the things I usually enjoy. My main issue is definitely just the constant worry and the physical tension that comes with it. It's the anxiety itself that feels so overwhelming.
Do you experience repetitive, unwanted thoughts or images that constantly pop into your mind, or feel driven to perform certain actions or rituals repeatedly to ease your anxiety?

No, I don't experience any repetitive rituals, compulsions, or specific unwanted images like that. It is more of a constant, uncontrollable worry about everyday life and future uncertainties that I just can't seem to stop.
How much does this constant worry and physical tension interfere with your daily life, such as your work, school, or relationships?

It interferes a great deal because my worries constantly surface, scattering my attention and making it incredibly hard to focus on my work or daily tasks. On top of that, the constant physical stiffness and muscle aches leave me feeling completely exhausted and uncomfortable throughout the day.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets all DSM-5 criteria for Generalized Anxiety Disorder: excessive, uncontrollable anxiety and worry about multiple areas of life (work, school, family, finances) for 11 months (exceeding the 6-month requirement), associated with muscle tension, easy fatigability, and difficulty concentrating. Other conditions like Major Depressive Disorder and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder have been ruled out through targeted questioning. I can now confidently finalize the diagnosis.
